name: Kolkata
shortDescription: Kolkata rewards slow travel through grand museums, riverfront ghats, book-lined streets, neighbourhood arts, historic institutions and deeply rooted Bengali food.
description:
Kolkata's character lives between formal monuments and ordinary streets. The Maidan and Victoria Memorial express the former imperial capital; North Kolkata preserves courtyard houses and cultural institutions; the Hooghly riverfront connects ghats, ferries and the engineering landmark of Howrah Bridge.

Allow three days if possible. Group the Maidan museums, take a separate north-city route through College Street and Jorasanko, and use a ferry for a river-level view rather than spending every journey in traffic. Metro, buses, local trains, ferries and taxis overlap, but no single mode covers everything.

Durga Puja transforms Kolkata into a vast public art festival, but also changes transport, accommodation and crowd conditions completely. Outside the festival, winter offers the easiest walking weather; summer and monsoon demand a slower rhythm.
bestTimeToVisit:
November to February provides cooler, drier conditions for long walks and food exploration. December and January evenings can feel cool by local standards.

March to May becomes hot and humid. June to September brings monsoon rain and possible waterlogging. Durga Puja usually falls in September or October and is extraordinary, but only visitors prepared for crowds, late nights and advance bookings should centre a first trip on it.
bestTimeToVisitShort: November to February; Durga Puja needs separate planning
budgetEstimate: ₹1,700–5,500 per person per day (excluding intercity travel)

topAttractions.name: Victoria Memorial
topAttractions.description: The marble monument and museum sit within landscaped Maidan grounds and introduce the city's colonial-era history through architecture and collections.
topAttractions.timings: Museum and gardens have separate schedules; verify

topAttractions.name: Indian Museum
topAttractions.description: Founded in 1814, this vast institution covers archaeology, art, geology and natural history. Choose priority galleries and check renovation closures.
topAttractions.timings: Usually closed Monday and some holidays; verify

topAttractions.name: Howrah Bridge and Mullick Ghat
topAttractions.description: The cantilever bridge and flower market below provide a powerful view of working Kolkata. Visit early, protect valuables and avoid obstructing traders.

topAttractions.name: Prinsep Ghat
topAttractions.description: A riverside promenade and Palladian memorial popular toward sunset, with views of the Vidyasagar Setu and access to private boat rides.

topAttractions.name: Jorasanko Thakur Bari
topAttractions.description: Rabindranath Tagore's ancestral home is now a museum within Rabindra Bharati University, offering context on the family and Bengal Renaissance.
topAttractions.timings: Verify museum days and university access

topAttractions.name: St Paul's Cathedral
topAttractions.description: A major Anglican cathedral beside the Maidan, noted for its Gothic Revival architecture and calm interior.

topAttractions.name: Kalighat Temple
topAttractions.description: An intensely active Shakti pilgrimage site rather than a conventional monument. Dress modestly and reject anyone promising privileged access.

topAttractions.name: Belur Math
topAttractions.description: The Ramakrishna Mission headquarters sits across the Hooghly in a spacious, contemplative campus. Combine it with a ferry or nearby Dakshineswar.

localFood.name: Kolkata Biryani
localFood.description: A fragrant, relatively subtle biryani traditionally distinguished by a large potato alongside meat and rice.

localFood.name: Kathi Roll
localFood.description: Skewered filling, egg, onions and sauces wrapped in paratha make one of the city's defining portable meals.

localFood.name: Macher Jhol
localFood.description: Bengali fish curry varies by fish, season and household, and is best understood as part of a complete rice meal.

localFood.name: Kosha Mangsho
localFood.description: Slow-cooked mutton in a dark, concentrated gravy, commonly paired with luchi or rice.

localFood.name: Mishti Doi and Sandesh
localFood.description: Set sweet yoghurt and fresh chhana sweets show Bengal's dairy-confectionery tradition without needing an elaborate meal.

localFood.name: Puchka
localFood.description: Kolkata's tamarind-forward version of filled crisp puri is assembled to order and has devoted neighbourhood followings.

tips: Use Metro for compatible north-south journeys and ferries for selected river crossings.
Yellow taxis and app cabs coexist; confirm the meter or app fare.
Build buffers around Howrah and Sealdah stations.
Book months ahead for Durga Puja and expect extensive walking.
Carry rain protection during monsoon and avoid deep waterlogging.
Winter is best for long heritage walks.
Ask before photographing Kumartuli artisans or ceremonies.
Use official temple queues and refuse access promises.
Watch belongings in markets, festivals and crowded transport.
Park Street is central for first visits.
Sudder Street has budget options of uneven quality.
Salt Lake and New Town suit business trips but are distant from heritage Kolkata.

hiddenGems: Kumartuli - A working potters' quarter where festival idols are made; visit respectfully and ask before photographing.
South Park Street Cemetery - An atmospheric eighteenth-century cemetery whose paths and monuments illuminate early colonial Kolkata.
Marble Palace - A private historic mansion with access arrangements that must be confirmed well ahead.
Kolkata tram remnants - Limited heritage operations can change; treat any ride as a bonus, not a fixed itinerary anchor.
Rabindra Sarobar - A southern lake and walking area best experienced in the morning.
Bow Barracks - A compact historic neighbourhood known for its Anglo-Indian community; remember it is residential, not an exhibit.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Kolkata?
faq.answer: Three days cover the principal museum, riverfront, north-city culture and food; four allows a slower neighbourhood rhythm.

faq.question: Is Durga Puja a good time for a first visit?
faq.answer: It is culturally exceptional but intensely crowded. Visit then only if the festival itself is your priority and book early.

faq.question: Are Kolkata's trams reliable for sightseeing?
faq.answer: Services and routes have changed significantly. Check current operations and never build an essential connection around a tram ride.

faq.question: What is the easiest way to see the Hooghly?
faq.answer: A public ferry crossing or a walk at Prinsep Ghat offers useful river views; private boats require an agreed route, fare and safe conditions.
